description:
## Problem
During the TPC-DS-OBT scale runs of 2026-11-10 query generation at SF 10000 and above failed: dsqgen timed out on Q9. The validator accepts values up to 100000 for `tpcds` and `tpcds_obt`, so the command line accepts scale factors at which query generation is known to fail. Whether plain `tpcds` fails the same way was not tested; it uses the same dsqgen.

## Change
Reproduce with dsqgen alone at SF 10000 for Q9, for both benchmarks, and find the cause (the timeout value, or a real hang). Then either fix query generation at that scale or lower the accepted maximum for the two benchmarks and say so in the error message and docs.

## Guardrails
- Query generation only; no data generation at these scales is needed to reproduce.
- A lower maximum is a user-visible change and needs a changelog fragment and the matching site docs edit.

## Decision gates
Determine Q9 query-generation timeout versus hang with dsqgen alone and bounded diagnostics, independently through tpcds and tpcds_obt entry points. The owner selected accepted range 0.01–100000: lowering it is a new owner decision, not an automatic fallback.

## Verification rubric
Pass: record binary/version, seed, timeout, output and cause at SF 10000 with smaller control and SF 100000 boundary. Accepted fix returns valid scale-sensitive SQL through both paths; a restricted maximum is allowed only with explicit approval and matching CLI/MCP/docs tests.

## Additional guardrails
No data generation at these scales, huge benchmark runs or arbitrary timeout inflation. Do not silently special-case Q9, substitute wrong-scale SQL, or claim both entry points work from only a raw binary test.
